doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Doing his own bookings; Europe dates and the Beirut engagement
summary: Walton enjoys booking himself without commissions, details upcoming Helsinki, Hamburg, London and Beirut dates, and Brower jokes about not wanting to go to Beirut.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Is it … are you at a point now where uh, you've heard so much music, you've played so much music that you pretty much don't need to um, where silence is of value to you?
Oh well, no.
And really just hear what you …what’s in your head?

Yeah, well you picture me as a man, as a person who uh, is, uh, totally involved in music. I'm also uh, totally involved … I have an office uh, at my residence, you know, that I do my own bookings. So that takes up a uh, uh, uh, you know, the emails? And different things like that. I have, I like to do that too. A lot of musicians don't, not only don't like to do it, they might even uh, it could be described as hating to do it. And uh, I find myself being attracted to this process of booking. And of course it eliminates uh, and makes the commissions impossible. And uh, I thought I'd give you a minute to uh, work on that one. [chuckles] But, uh, so uh, but I mean I have, I don't mind it …
The Co-Mission Impossible part.

[chuckles] Yeah. Uh, I, I don't mind an agency booking me somewhere. That's entirely … and in fact sometime I have to call if I have a hole in my schedule. For instance, in November I'm going uh, uh to Europe, uh, first gig is in Helsinki. There's a Birdland there. And there's one in Hamburg. And then we, we uh, we segue into London at Ronnie Scott's. So uh, that one I can do, I can do. I can't do that within my office, except to call Mary Scott who was the wife of Ronnie Scott. She lives two blocks from me, and she, she arranges those gigs. Am I digressing again?
[inaudible]

Well that's what I do, do, besides listen to music, deal with music all the time. I deal with my schedule which is [inaudible] on October uh, 13, 14, 15, I'm playin' at a place uh, in uh, uh, it's called Beirut in Lebanon. So, that, that takes some doing, you know, uh, uh, different permits and things like that, contracts and uh …
Well, I was actually interested in working with you until you said ‘Beirut’ so that conversation is over.
[laughs]
[inaudible].
Oh yeah, that's, that's a no-no? I shouldn't … I should …
No, it's good for you. [inaudible]
Oh. But, you wouldn't go there.
Probably not.
Yeah, well, tell me why you wouldn't go, if you don't mind.
I’m afraid shit might happen. Is that on tape?
Oh my God.
[not understandable] [laughs]
Yeah, I, I've thought of that too.
I mean I have a friend who does USO Tours all the time.
Oh.
Don't you want to go to Iraq with me? Or go …
Oh no, no. Iraq … I don't think Iraq is a, is a good idea.
I prefer my living room.
Right. Well, I've agreed to it now, taken the deposit, so I gotta go. So uh, if you …
Are you required to return it? [inaudible]
[laughs] No, this is about the air ticket.
